decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with left arm toward the small left toy car; plan cars in blue, cameras in red, watches in white. Geometry and grasp height will be refined from wrist RGB.
Align open left gripper over the light-blue car and descend gradually, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Use wrist view to advance the fingers around the taxi body, lower a little, and close. Retention remains to be checked by lifting.
Lift the closed left gripper to verify taxi retention, then carry it above the left side of the blue basket.
Taxi was not retained in the lift. Reopen and return for a lower, slightly rearward grasp; reduce increments after the continuity rejection.
Close around the taxi at the lower contact height, pause for closure, and make a short vertical retention test.
Taxi remains visually between the fingers after lifting. Carry upward and forward toward the left half of the blue basket, keeping the grasp closed.
Place the retained taxi over the blue basket, open and retreat. Begin a separate elbow-up approach with the right arm toward the red car.
After the left continuity guard, avoid further forward reach. Lower slightly at the current position over blue, release the taxi, and retract. Continue gradual right-arm preparation.
Taxi is released inside blue. Retract the left arm clear while aligning the right gripper across the red car's narrow dimension, descending toward a pregrasp.
Fine-align and lower around the red car, close and test a short lift. Concurrently approach the left silver watch with the left gripper open.
Lift the red car toward blue while checking retention. Lower around the silver watch's band, close the left gripper, and make a brief lift test.
Both objects appear retained. Carry the silver watch toward white and position the red car fully over blue, using small forward increments near the baskets.
Right car appears against the basket rim; back away and lift while reorienting for more forward fingertip reach. Place the left watch into white and release only after advancing inside.
The red car is back on the table, so reapproach it open with jaws across its width. Move left clear of the released silver watch toward the central black watch.
Use wrist alignment to center the black watch under the left hand. Back the right hand off the blue rim, lower around the red car and close before another retention test.
Close around the centered black watch after a small descent. The right car grasp was blocked at its roof; reopen, steepen the approach and recenter before lowering again.
Lift the black watch and turn to a shallower carrying angle for basket reach. Shift the open right jaws rearward off the blue rim and around the car, then close.
Black watch is retained; carry it toward white at a shallower angle. Right fingers closed over the car rather than around it: reopen, lift, correct the grasp center rightward/backward, then descend.
Correct the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Reapproach the silver watch while closing the centered red-car grasp and testing a vertical lift.
Car is now visually lifted between the right fingers. Raise and rotate it to a forward-reaching carrying orientation. Move left backward away from the basket rim toward the watch face.

The red car was not retained through rotation. Reorient the empty right gripper near-vertical for a central grasp, then carry without rotating. Center and close on the silver watch, checking a short lift.

Both previous grasps appear too high or off-center. Open, lower the left jaws onto the watch band rather than its empty center, and align the right jaws with the car center using the rotated wrist view. Close at the corrected height.
The corrected jaws visibly surround both objects. Keep them fully closed and make a slow vertical lift without orientation changes to check retention and clear the basket rim.
Silver watch is securely retained in the lift; carry it farther inside white without rotating. Red car was not retained; open and adjust rearward/rightward with a shallower, lower approach.
Advance the retained watch well inside white, lower and release. Back the right gripper off the blue rim and partially narrow its opening before lowering around the red car.
Silver watch has been released inside white. Retract left toward the black watch. Close the right gripper at the lower, rim-cleared car grasp and lift without rotating.

The car remains on the table below the closed fingers; reopen and lower substantially to its sidewalls rather than roof height. Move left backward and down to bring the black watch face between its fingers.
Close both at the corrected low contact height and lift vertically without changing orientation. Inspect whether the objects actually follow rather than relying on gripper command state.
Carry the black watch toward white without wrist rotation. Lift the right-hand car higher and slightly clear of the rim before any sideways transport; retention is still uncertain.
Neither object survived transport. Recenter left on the black watch's solid body, not the band edge. Switch right to the unobstructed front camera; the car needs a later rim-clear approach.
Center the black watch's solid housing in the left pinch and close at low height. Lower the right hand toward the front camera while correcting its lateral alignment from wrist RGB.
Shift the left pinch onto the watch housing rather than its edge and reclose. Lower and center the right gripper around the camera body, close, then test both with a small vertical lift.
Back the left grasp slightly off the basket lip, then lift without rotating. Lift the camera vertically as well; keep both grippers closed and check RGB for actual retention.
The camera follows the right hand in RGB; carry it toward red without rotating. The watch stayed on the table, so switch left to a near-vertical approach over its solid housing.
Keep the camera closed while moving it inside red, lower, then release. Use the left wrist view to advance toward the watch housing with the vertical gripper open.

Allow the camera to settle in red and retreat to the remaining right camera. The left watch approach is obstructed by white's rim; switch left to the accessible camera and restore a shallower grasp angle.
Center and lower the left gripper around its camera, then close. Back the right hand away from red's front rim to align over the remaining camera and descend toward its sidewalls.
Lift the left camera without changing orientation and begin moving it toward a central handoff staging point. Fine-align and close around the right camera, then make a vertical retention test.
Right camera is visibly retained; lift it clear and carry toward red. Left camera stayed on the table: reopen and recenter on its body rather than its left corner, then lower for a new grasp.
Place the second camera deeper inside red and open. Advance the left pinch toward the remaining camera's center, close below its upper surface, and test lifting before transport.
Two cameras are visibly in red. Lift and carry the remaining left camera toward a central table staging point without rotating; retract the right arm clear of the basket for the subsequent pickup.
The left camera is retained in RGB. Continue to the left edge of the central staging area while keeping the right hand separated and retracted; release will follow after lowering.
Lower the retained camera onto the central table near the workspace boundary, open, and start withdrawing left. Keep the right arm stationary until the staging placement is clear.
Withdraw the left arm fully into its workspace. Bring the open right hand toward the staged camera at the center boundary, with a modest inward finger direction while keeping its EE on the right.

The staged camera settled slightly left of center. Angle the right fingers inward while keeping its EE positive-x, and descend toward it; left remains well separated and approaches the black watch again.
Fine-adjust the right pinch inward over the staged camera and close at a lower height. Advance the left open fingers toward the black watch, checking for basket-rim interference before closing.
Lift the staged camera into the right workspace with its orientation fixed. Advance the left fingers onto the black watch housing, lower slightly, close, and test a short lift.

Both objects now remain visibly between the fingers. Lift the black watch slightly back from white's lip before moving forward. Carry the camera toward red with fixed wrist orientation and closed grippers.

The black watch is retained; move it fully inside white before releasing. The camera slipped onto the central table, now in the right workspace; return open and restore the successful forward-facing grasp orientation.
Lower and release the retained black watch inside white, then withdraw. Recenter the right hand backward and leftward over the last camera and descend with open fingers.
Both placed watches are visibly inside white. Retract left clear while closing around the centered camera and lifting vertically without changing the right wrist orientation.

The camera remains between the right fingers after lifting. Carry it slowly toward red with orientation fixed; move the left arm back toward its home configuration while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Keep the last camera closed and raise it clear of red's front rim while moving above the basket. Complete the left arm's gradual return toward its initial pose.
Lower the retained third camera inside red, open, and let it settle. Then retreat rightward and backward toward the last silver watch; keep left parked.
All three cameras are visible inside red. Approach the remaining right-side silver watch with open fingers, maintaining the current elbow-up and wrist orientation.
Use the right wrist view to move backward and lower around the silver watch, aiming for the solid face and band rather than closing above it. Leave the left arm parked.
Center the right pinch across the watch band, close at low height, and lift without rotation. Begin an elbow-up preparation of the left arm for a later center-table handoff.
The silver watch remains against the right fingers after lifting. Carry it slowly inward with fixed orientation and closed grasp, while preparing the left hand at a safely separated position.
Watch retention is now confirmed by its fixed position in the right wrist view during translation. Continue toward the central staging area with the left hand waiting clear.
Lower the retained silver watch onto the central table near the workspace boundary and open for a staged transfer. Keep the left hand stationary until the right has withdrawn.
Withdraw the open right hand into its own workspace so the watch can settle. Approach the staged watch with the left hand, keeping the arms separated and its EE left of center.

Align the left fingers over the staged silver watch while keeping its EE left of center. Prepare the right hand above the red car with jaws oriented across its narrow width, staying clear of the basket rim.
Close on the staged silver watch and lift without rotation. Level the right jaw-closing axis to horizontal and approach the red car with a reduced opening to avoid the nearby basket lip.
Test watch retention with a higher lift and a slow leftward carry. Lift the right fingers clear, correct the car's lateral offset in the wrist view, then lower with level jaws and reduced opening.
The watch slipped onto the table; reopen and realign for a lower centered grasp. Close the right fingers and draw back gently to move the car away from the obstructing basket lip before another lift.

Close the centered watch grasp after a small lowering and test a vertical lift. The car did not move with the closed right hand; reopen, recenter forward, and descend further to its sidewalls before closing again.

The watch appears retained by its housing; carry slowly toward white without rotating. The right grasp is obstructed at the car/rim, so draw straight back at the observed height to clear the lip and check whether the car follows.

Carry the retained silver watch to white with its grasp unchanged. Return the right pinch to the car center with level jaws, limited opening, and a lower sidewall grasp height rather than closing above the roof.
Release the third watch inside white and withdraw. The right car approach is obstructed, so lift the closed fingers above it and move to its basket-facing side for a gentle backward repositioning.

All watches are visible inside white. Return left gradually toward home. Lower the closed right fingertips beside the car and gently draw it backward away from the basket lip before attempting another grasp.
Finish returning the left arm toward home. Reopen and center the right jaws slightly forward over the car, then lower to the sidewalls with the jaw axis level to avoid the basket lip.
Use much smaller left increments after the continuity rejection. Center the right pinch slightly forward, close around the car, pause, and lift vertically to assess actual retention.
The car remains on the table. Reopen to a rim-clearing width, shift the pinch from the hood toward the cabin, and lower farther to the sidewalls before closing.
A finger is contacting the car roof rather than passing its side. Use that contact for a slow backward repositioning away from the basket lip, keeping the opening fixed and monitoring the result.
